title: The Lost Bus
synopsis: A school bus, twenty-two children, and a wildfire that has already eaten the only road home. You are driving. Don't look in the mirror.

nodes.text: The sky over the school is the wrong color — a brown-orange you've only seen at sunset, and it's noon. The dispatcher's voice cracks: "Get them out, now." Twenty-two kids file onto your bus, too quiet.

choices.text: Take the highway, the fast way
choices.consequence: Speed is safety until it isn't. You take the highway, the fast way. The decision moves you toward The Highway and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

choices.text: Take the ridge road, the long way
choices.consequence: The longer road is sometimes the only road. You take the ridge road, the long way. The decision moves you toward The Ridge Road and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

choices.text: Wait for the convoy to form up
choices.consequence: There is strength in numbers and danger in delay. You choose to wait for the convoy to form up. It opens the route to The Convoy, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: The on-ramp is a parking lot of brake lights and ash. Embers the size of fists drift across the windshield. A boy named Marcus asks if his house is okay. You don't know how to lie to a child.

choices.text: Tell him the truth, gently
choices.consequence: Children survive honesty better than we think. You tell him the truth, gently. The decision moves you toward The Wall of Smoke and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

choices.text: Tell him everyone's going to be fine
choices.consequence: A kind lie can be a kind of bridge. You choose to tell him everyone's going to be fine. It opens the route to Marcus Knows, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: The ridge gives you a view you'll never unsee: the whole valley below is a sheet of moving fire, and it is climbing. But up here the road is clear. For now. To choose “Push the bus faster on the gravel” means meeting The Wall of Smoke; “Slow down for the blind curves” sends you toward The Lead Vehicle instead.

choices.text: Push the bus faster on the gravel
choices.consequence: Trade traction for time and pray. You commit to push the bus faster on the gravel. By The Wall of Smoke, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

choices.text: Slow down for the blind curves
choices.consequence: A controlled bus is a living bus. You commit to slow down for the blind curves. By The Lead Vehicle, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: Three other buses and a fire crew gather in the lot. The captain shouts orders, but there's no time and no consensus — and the smoke is already thickening at the fence line. The paths divide here: “Break from the convoy and go alone” leads into The Ridge Road, while “Follow the fire crew's lead vehicle” makes The Lead Vehicle the next reckoning.

choices.text: Break from the convoy and go alone
choices.consequence: Sometimes the group is just a slower target. You commit to break from the convoy and go alone. By The Ridge Road, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

choices.text: Follow the fire crew's lead vehicle
choices.consequence: Trust the people who run toward this. You choose to follow the fire crew's lead vehicle. It opens the route to The Lead Vehicle, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: The road vanishes into a gray nothing. Your headlights die against it. A girl in the front seat takes your sleeve. "I can't see," she says, and neither can you. “Crawl forward at walking pace” draws you toward The Bridge; “Stop and wait for the smoke to shift” leaves Trapped waiting on the other side.

choices.text: Crawl forward at walking pace
choices.consequence: Faith in a road you can't see is the whole job. You choose to crawl forward at walking pace. It opens the route to The Bridge, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

choices.text: Stop and wait for the smoke to shift
choices.consequence: Stillness in a fire is a terrible gamble. You commit to stop and wait for the smoke to shift. By Trapped, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: Marcus looks out the window at his street going by, the flames already in it, and stops asking questions. His silence is louder than any scream. The other kids feel it spread. The paths divide here: “Get them singing to break the fear” leads into The Animal on the Road, while “Give Marcus a job to do” makes Trapped the next reckoning.

choices.text: Get them singing to break the fear
choices.consequence: Noise is a rope thrown to the drowning. You choose to get them singing to break the fear. It opens the route to The Animal on the Road, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

choices.text: Give Marcus a job to do
choices.consequence: Purpose is the antidote to panic. You choose to give Marcus a job to do. It opens the route to Trapped, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: A deer stands frozen in your high beams, flanks heaving, a refugee like the rest of you. Behind it the brush is already glowing. The kids press to the windows. Choose “Edge around it and keep moving” and The Bridge comes into view; choose “Lean on the horn to send it running” and the road bends toward Through the Gap.

choices.text: Edge around it and keep moving
choices.consequence: Mercy is a luxury the fire doesn't grant. You edge around it and keep moving. The decision moves you toward The Bridge and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

choices.text: Lean on the horn to send it running
choices.consequence: Save what you can, even what isn't yours to save. You choose to lean on the horn to send it running. It opens the route to Through the Gap, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: You follow the fire truck's taillights like a prayer. Then it turns down a side road and is gone, and a downed power line writhes across the path ahead, throwing sparks. The distance between The Bridge and The Detour begins with the choice between “Drive over the line fast” and “Find another way around.”

choices.text: Drive over the line fast
choices.consequence: Rubber tires, steady nerves, no brakes. You choose to drive over the line fast. It opens the route to The Bridge, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

choices.text: Find another way around
choices.consequence: Respect the things that can kill you sideways. You choose to find another way around. It opens the route to The Detour, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: Through the smoke: a bridge, the only crossing for miles, and it's already burning at the far end. The fire hasn't reached the deck yet. You have maybe ninety seconds. The distance between Through the Gap and The River Ford begins with the choice between “Floor it across the bridge” and “Reverse and find the old ford downstream.”

choices.text: Floor it across the bridge
choices.consequence: Hesitation is the only thing that can't survive here. You commit to floor it across the bridge. By Through the Gap, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

choices.text: Reverse and find the old ford downstream
choices.consequence: Water is a road too, if you're brave enough. You choose to reverse and find the old ford downstream. It opens the route to The River Ford, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: The fire flanks you — there's flame on both shoulders now and the heat is warping the air. A child is crying without sound. The radio is just static and someone, somewhere, screaming a road name.

choices.text: Shelter in place and seal the bus
choices.consequence: When you can't outrun it, you outlast it. You commit to shelter in place and seal the bus. By Shelter in Place, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

choices.text: Make a run for the reservoir clearing
choices.consequence: One gap in the wall is all you need. You choose to make a run for the reservoir clearing. It opens the route to Through the Gap, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: The side road is barely a road — washboard dirt narrowing into trees that are starting to torch one by one, like matches in a row. But it bends away from the worst of it. The paths divide here: “Commit to the detour fully” leads into The River Ford, while “Turn back toward the highway after all” makes Smoke in the Cabin the next reckoning.

choices.text: Commit to the detour fully
choices.consequence: You choose to commit to the detour fully. It opens the route to The River Ford, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

choices.text: Turn back toward the highway after all
choices.consequence: Sometimes retreat is the only advance. You turn back toward the highway after all. The decision moves you toward Smoke in the Cabin and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: Smoke is seeping through the old door seals now, and a small voice in the back starts to cough, then another. The air inside the bus is becoming the thing you were driving away from.

choices.text: Seal the vents and ride it out
choices.consequence: Trap the good air and hoard it like gold. You commit to seal the vents and ride it out. By Shelter in Place, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

choices.text: Make a hard run for clearer air
choices.consequence: Outrun the cloud or become it. You make a hard run for clearer air. The decision moves you toward Through the Gap and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: There's a seam in the fire — a corridor of merely terrible heat between two walls of worse. It's closing. The bus groans up to speed. The kids have stopped making any sound at all. “Drive straight through the corridor” opens the route to The Far Side. “Use the reservoir to wet the bus first” changes the terms and carries you toward Shelter in Place.

choices.text: Drive straight through the corridor
choices.consequence: Aim at the gap and refuse to blink. You drive straight through the corridor. The decision moves you toward The Far Side and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

choices.text: Use the reservoir to wet the bus first
choices.consequence: A soaked machine buys a few precious degrees. You use the reservoir to wet the bus first. The decision moves you toward Shelter in Place and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: The old crossing is low water over smooth stone. The far bank is dark — unburned. But the current is faster than it looks and the bus is heavy with frightened cargo. “Ease across the ford slowly” opens the route to The Far Side. “Power across before the engine drowns” changes the terms and carries you toward Engine Trouble.

choices.text: Ease across the ford slowly
choices.consequence: Read the water like a road. You ease across the ford slowly. The decision moves you toward The Far Side and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

choices.text: Power across before the engine drowns
choices.consequence: Momentum is a kind of buoyancy. You power across before the engine drowns. The decision moves you toward Engine Trouble and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: You park in the reservoir clearing, kill the engine, tape the vents, and have the kids lie on the floor under coats. The fire arrives like a freight train made of weather. Then it passes, roaring, over and around.

choices.text: Wait until the heat truly breaks
choices.consequence: Patience is the bravest thing in a furnace. You commit to wait until the heat truly breaks. By The Count, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

choices.text: Move the moment the front passes
choices.consequence: The window after the wave is narrow and real. You commit to move the moment the front passes. By Engine Trouble, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: The bus bursts out of the smoke into clear gray air. Behind you the world is ending; ahead, impossibly, a road sign, intact, pointing toward town. A few kids start to cry — the good kind.

choices.text: Radio your survivors' count to dispatch
choices.consequence: Every name said aloud is a name saved. You commit to radio your survivors' count to dispatch. By The Count, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

choices.text: Push on without stopping
choices.consequence: Don't trust safety until you're standing in it. You push on without stopping. The decision moves you toward Town Lights and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: The bus coughs, sputters, and the temperature needle pins red. You're almost clear — almost. Steam rolls from under the hood. Twenty-two kids, one dying engine, and not quite enough road. To choose “Nurse it forward in low gear” means meeting Town Lights; “Stop and lead the kids out on foot” sends you toward One More Run instead.

choices.text: Nurse it forward in low gear
choices.consequence: Coax the machine like a frightened animal. You choose to nurse it forward in low gear. It opens the route to Town Lights, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

choices.text: Stop and lead the kids out on foot
choices.consequence: When the metal fails, the legs decide. You stop and lead the kids out on foot. The decision moves you toward One More Run and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: You make them line up and count off the way you've practiced a hundred bored mornings. “Drive the last miles to the shelter” opens the route to Town Lights. “Stop to help another stranded vehicle” changes the terms and carries you toward One More Run.

choices.text: Drive the last miles to the shelter
choices.consequence: The end of the road is the start of the rest. You drive the last miles to the shelter. The decision moves you toward Town Lights and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

choices.text: Stop to help another stranded vehicle
choices.consequence: There's always one more name to save. You commit to stop to help another stranded vehicle. By One More Run, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: The shelter parking lot is full of flashing lights and reaching arms. Parents run at the bus before it's fully stopped. You open the door and a wall of crying, hugging, breathing humanity pours in.

choices.text: Hand each child to someone who loves them
choices.consequence: This is the only paperwork that matters. You hand each child to someone who loves them. The decision moves you toward Everyone Home and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

choices.text: Go back out for the ones still on the mountain
choices.consequence: Heroes are just people who can't sit still. You go back out for the ones still on the mountain. The decision moves you toward One More Run and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: Empty now, the bus feels enormous. The fire's glow still pulses to the east, and the radio is full of names of roads, of children, of people not yet counted. Your hands are shaking. The engine is still warm.

choices.text: Turn around and drive back in
choices.consequence: The bravest tank is the one that's nearly empty. You choose to turn around and drive back in. It opens the route to The Second Trip, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

choices.text: Stay, rest, let the crews take it
choices.consequence: You can't pour from a tank that's run dry. You choose to stay, rest, let the crews take it. It opens the route to The Weight You Carry, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: Twenty-two children, twenty-two reunions. You don't remember driving back to the depot. Months later a kid you don't recognize hugs your knees in a grocery store and won't let go, and you finally, quietly, fall apart in the cereal aisle.

You go back in. Of course you do. The mountain is a cathedral of fire and you drive into it because somewhere up there is someone's whole world, waiting on a roadside. They never give medals for the trips that count. You don't want one.

You let the crews take the next run, and for the rest of your life you wonder about it — not with guilt exactly, but with the quiet arithmetic of a person who did enough and will never quite believe it. The kids you saved grow up. That has to be the answer. It is.
